This episode differs from the 2006-2007 period because modern post-Dodd-Frank capital frameworks provide a direct, explicit regulatory instrument—the CCyB itself—which did not exist then, making activation a matter of policy switch rather than structural overhaul. It differs from the 2017-2019 debate because the current cycle has been preceded by rapid, pandemic-era asset price inflation followed by sustained high interest rates that have exposed hidden duration and credit risks in commercial real estate and regional banking portfolios. These historical parallels show that once regulators perceive a disconnect between benign reported losses and underlying asset vulnerability, they shift toward preemptive buffer accumulation.
